frequency_question: How often do announced sector-specific tariff threats proceed to actual implementation rather than being deferred, rescinded, or resolved via a last-minute deal within the designated window?
membership_rule: Includes formal executive announcements of specific tariff rates on specific partner country goods with explicit implementation dates under trade authority statutes. Excludes general campaign rhetoric not codified into formal scheduled implementation actions.

coverage_note: 4 named major bilateral tariff showdowns with scheduled deadlines; representing the relevant class of high-stakes leverage threats.
known_gaps: Excludes broad multilateral tariff campaigns (like broad China Section 301 tranches) which follow different negotiation dynamics than single-partner border leverage threats.
skeleton: Threatened bilateral tariff actions with set deadlines divided into those that execute on schedule versus those averted by negotiated pauses or withdrawals.
multiplier: 2 hits out of 4 named comparable historical showdowns with close allies/trading partners
validity_reason: The base rate reflects executive trade negotiation tactics which remain stable across modern administrations utilizing tariff threats as leverage, valid until executive trade authorities or statutory frameworks undergo major legislative overhaul.
